newsitem.title: FRANCE: French voters' intention poll due later today-CSA.
newsitem.headline: French voters' intention poll due later today-CSA.

text.p: An opinion poll of French voters' intentions, conducted after President Jacques Chirac on Monday called a snap election for May 25 and June 1, will probably be released later today, French polling organisation CSA Institute said on Tuesday.
A CSA official told Reuters the poll was being conducted now and would be released as soon as it was completed. He was unable to give a precise time for the release.
An official at the BVA polling organisation said it would be doing a poll "very soon" and expected to publish the results at the "beginning of next week".

He said BVA's last opinion poll would be published one week before the first round of voting on May 25. He also said confidential polls may be taken between the first and second round of voting on June 1 but French law prevented it from publishing the results.
Louis Harris said its first poll would probably appear at the beginning of next week although there was a possibility a poll might be released later this week.
An IFOP official was not able to say yet when its first poll of voters' intentions would be published.
IPSOS said it had no plans to conduct any independent polls and declined to say who had ordered polls or when they would be published.
Officials at polling organisation Sofres were not immediately available for comment.
